Surely you're not suggesting that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: On line 40 -- 14 on page 86 it says something which I do not think you wanted to say I think you spoke about eradication and here it says ratification. So it turns the meaning around I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps -- one of the disadvantages with this -- this podium, but I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm not saying ratification. Erad -- I mean, they're trying to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- right?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Own and Stoltenberg were not calling for the eradication of the state. They did seem to be seeking some solution; that would be a three republic within the borders, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And do you think -- do you know whether there might have been some sort of earlier plan going back as early as 1992 that might have had something like that in mind?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Even prior to the Vance-Owen Plan?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that Lord Carrington might have been involved in that and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There you go?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- That was the reference I was going to give you earlier about an English Lord having a governmental position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Okay. I met the gentleman. He's a -- has had an incredible career. All right. So now that we've clarified that, if we could go further down on the issue of helicopters, because you indicated yesterday that you might have raised it -- you might have raised this issue with Mr. Prlic, and here concretely you said: "Prlic said that he did not agree with the civilian demonstration (resulting in the seizure of the helicopters) as a means of exerting pressure and as a result had refused to be drawn into internal negotiations on the issue." So it would appear that Dr. Jadranko Prlic had in fact stated his position with respect to the helicopters; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it would seem to me from reading all sorts of other documents that have been presented here, your initiative was with Boban to try to get him to -- to release these two helicopters.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. We very much saw that this was Mate Boban's hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And if I might just add briefly, and I know you're up against time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Go ahead?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hence this continual interest of ours about the relationship between the forming government and the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And do you think that it might have helped you a little bit in hindsight, of course, and I understand this was a war and I'm not picking on you but -- but do you think, in hindsight, it might have been helpful for you to have actually seen what existed of the legislation that made it possible for the existence of the Croatian Community and how that community evolved into the Croatian republic so then you might be able to understand at least as of 31st October 1993 de jure, legally speaking, where the powers lay?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In retrospect it would have been. You're right to draw the attention to the fact there was a war going on and a number of other issues we were dealing with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- okay. I think that was -- that was that. With -- and then we talked about Stupni Do already, and I believe yesterday you indicated that Mr. -- there was a document shown to you where it said that Mr. Prlic had condemned the -- the atrocity; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in this particular document we also see that he is -- he is stating a position or opinion that those responsible were removed and some action is -- is under way.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'd have to just quickly look at the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Go ahead, look at it.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it in the same --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah, it's in the same paragraph.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And one of the things that I gleaned from reading the material and listening to you as well was that when you were meeting with Dr. Jadranko Prlic, and others as well, they seem -- he in particular seemed to be wanting information from you, the international, as to what was happening in other parts of Herceg-Bosna or Central Bosnia, because he had limited or no access to that information or what was happening over there; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what made meeting with Mr. Prlic always so interesting because it was much more discussions and, yes, he was particularly interested soon after my arrival to get a clearer understanding of the situation in Central Bosnia. What I wouldn't necessarily agree with is that he -- and certainly wouldn't agree with it, that he would have had no information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe that was an overstatement, but certainly he's asking you what is happening because you were in a better position to know what happening than he was.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd come fresh from territory that he hadn't been able to visit for over a year, and he was also -- just to give you the complete answer with regards to the EU, yes, he was -- he was interested in what the international community thought. There were many dimensions to the discussion. Often you would have a discussion with somebody and it would be question asked and restricted question response. We had a broad engagement with Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And Mr. Prlic, as I understand that -- from listening to you, his -- his primary concerns or his preoccupation was with setting up the political structure.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do remember him saying that he'd written constitutions before and he would be writing another one now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So although his background I believe was economics --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Would it surprise you, sir, if I were to tell you that no constitution was ever drafted?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wouldn't surprise me. It would perhaps account for the some of the confusion as to exactly what it was, but no constitution being drafted doesn't stop a functioning government.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would point you to the United Kingdom that doesn't have a written constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. A fine example. Now -- now, do you know exactly about his particular position? Do you know what -- how it functioned, where -- what his actual powers and responsibilities and authorities were, aside from what you might have heard by others and what you might have thought, because he is a rather charismatic individual, comes across fairly well, speaks good English. So did you actually know for a fact?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew for a fact that his title was the president of the government. First of all president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and as you'll see, it seemed that from what he was telling us and what subsequently emerged that he was going to be the president or, if you like, the Prime Minister of the government. So did I know that? Well, I heard it from him. It was correlated by other information, and I never heard him suggest anything other than that was his title.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But -- all right. Now, before we get to the documents, because I'm told that we need to get to documents, you say that he was the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. If he was that, what was Mate Boban?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mate Boban was the president, yes. Maybe I should have said the president of the government of Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Very well. All right. Let's go through some documents very quickly because that's what we need to do. If we could look at P 04611.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, are we still --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, we're on my documents right now.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The blue binders.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The blue binder?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may be being dim here, sorry. Yeah, got it. Got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Otherwise, we can help you out here.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It is -- now, if we look at the second page, we'll see that there is a date to it, 28 August 1993. The first page is -- is the preamble, and if we could -- I take it you've seen this document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't know if you have the version in Croatian, but -- all right. And we could see from the very first page it's published in Official Gazette of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, October 1993, so that would have been about the time that you were in and around the Mostar area; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And You would agree that an Official Gazette si something -- or maybe you don't know. I'm assuming a fact at this point, but perhaps you could help us whether the Official Gazette is something that is widely circulated and available to the public so they know what's in it? Do you know if that's the case or not?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For the Court's benefit, it's paragraph 3, the last part of that paragraph may be of some interest. I don't want to spend too much time reading it, but I'm talking about where it says, "future federation of republics and by agreeing to participate in joint institutions and services of mutual interest in Bosnia-Herzegovina." That's the portion I wish to draw to the Court's attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: By the way, at this point in time do you know whether there is discussion in Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Muslims and the Serbs of also having joint institutions, also having -- forming their own republics?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you -- sorry, could you orient me just so I don't get lost on the track of -- I could not find what you were referring to there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is the first paragraph on the very first page, the preamble: "Having found that the existing political and state system does not ensure does not ensure them their rights in Bosnia-Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- and their rights -- okay -- and their rights to Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Croat -- the Croatian people are determined to defend these rights by, among other things, changing their status and establishing their own state community in a part of the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina by transferring a part of their constitutive rights to the future federation of republics and by agreeing to participate in certain joint institutions," and so on. That's the part I wanted to point out. Obviously, you would not -- since you haven't seen this, you wouldn't be aware of this, but if I could draw your attention to the following page. Following page, we see that this is a basic decision on establishing and proclaiming the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. What we read was the preamble. If we go to article 3 very quickly, we see that it says: "The republics shall be the integral and indivisible democratic state of the Croatian people in," in, I underscore that for the Judges, "in Bosnia-Herzegovina founded on human rights and liberties, the rule of law and social justice." Now, from this it would appear that -- at least this basic decision, we're talking about being inside Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. I'm just going to go on. Okay. If we go to Article 6 we talk about a state: "The state authority shall be organised on the principles of parliamentary democracy." And then it talks about the legislative authority, the executive authority, and the judicial authority. So from here it appears that had you or your staff had available this Official Gazette, you would at least on paper understand how this republic was being formed; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I do believe that our own inquiries are reaching similar conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that, but I'm just saying --

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm just pointing this out, okay?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been helpful I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. And since we're losing time, I point to the Court also to Article 7 and Article 11. That's all for this document. If we go to the next document, and that would be P 04589.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, from the top of the page we see Mostar, 11 October, 1993. This is Official Gazette of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, and this is a decision on constituting the house of representatives of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, and if we look at the next page we see that the date of 28 August 1993. So again based on this we see that there was legislation available in and around Mostar at that point in time, and we -- also Article 2 might be important to the Judges. I take it you were not availed of this. You were not aware of this?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have this or whatever. I would love to ask Mr. Prlic why he didn't give me a copy. It would have helped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you should have asked. Now -- because -- and I don't mean this in a very flippant way, but surely a gentleman such as Dr. Jadranko Prlic who would actually take you there in your white uniform, probably to the dismay of some of the others that were there, because it appeared from your testimony that you were more or less his -- his invited guest but others weren't welcoming your presence, he wasn't the kind of person that would hide this sort of information from you.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. We shouldn't chastise him for this omission.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. P 05517.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And this is a summary, Your Honours, I bring to your attention, at the very top. It appears that this summary was provided by the office of the Prosecution, and this is from the Official Gazette again, October 1, 1993. If we flip -- go to the second page, Your Honours, you will see that it says there: "Law on government of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna." And then Article 4 says: "The House of Representatives of the HR HB --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. It is only a technical, I would say, correction. You mentioned here that the Official Gazette, October 1, 1993, but I believe it is October 7th. On the second page we will find the date, which is correct, the 7th or probably even later on. It was number 1, but October, something like --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: That kind of date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're right, Your Honour. I saw the 1 and the comma and I assumed -- you're absolutely right. But it was October 1993, and thank you for bringing that to our attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On Article 4 on the second page we see: "The House of Representatives of the HR HB at the proposal of president of HR HB appoints and releases president and members of government." So there we see at least the functions, so one of the functions of the house of representatives. And then of course Article 7 talks about a no-confidence vote. Again, you did not have that available to you?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And if we go to the last page we see it's 30 September 1993, Mostar. So that's one minor detail, but nonetheless it's there. Now if we could go to P 06583.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I want to point out that I'm being told, Your Honours, that there should be a correction in the translation of this document. This is a statement. If we go to the second page, we see that it's dated 10 November 1993, office of the president of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. Then if we go to the first page, we see that it says in the very first paragraph that Mate Boban has appointed Jadranko Prlic Prime Minister, and then it goes on: "At the Prime Minister's suggestion the following people were appointed." I'm told this should be "nominated." Perhaps the translators could verify that if the document is on B/C/S on the e-court, but it says nominated members of the government as opposed to appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take it you were not aware of this statement?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, this an example of the sort of thing that we did get, a single sheet, but I can't be sure I saw that. Interesting, but we'd have to look back at my dates as to when I identified particular positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right okay?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this is the sort, just like that one I referred to, HDZ, we did see. So not the detail behind it but the announcement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right if we go to P 06772.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Again it says at the top Your Honours that that is a summary. This is something provided to us by the Office of the Prosecution and I'm told again there should be some corrections. Where it says "decision," it should be on the election of the president, deputy president, and members of government as opposed to what it says now which says, "on the election of the Prime Minister, deputy Prime Minister and cabinet members." Also, I'm told that it should say rather than, "the Chamber of Deputies," it should say the house of representatives, "elected the following," and then you see who is elected. And then at the very end it's signed by the vice-president of the House of Representatives and not the deputy speaker of the Chamber of Deputies. Were you aware of this decision, sir?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not this decision, but it --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I just add one little thing?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are just occasionally name changes against the titles. I would draw your attention to the health minister, Dr. Ivan Bagaric changes to Ivan Saric, and I think this is indicative of the sorts of fluidity I was discussing earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may be another example. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. The next document is P 07424, and you briefly touched upon this yesterday and I thought this might be interesting for the Trial Chamber. This is a decision on the establishment of the presidential council of the Republic of Herceg-Bosna, and if we flip to the second page we see that the date is 10 December 1993, and since we're on this page, if we look at paragraph number 4, it says, "The presidential council shall deal with strategic, political, and defence matters and shall coordinate the activities of the executive bodies of the republic." Do you see that? So this tells us a little bit what this presidential council is supposed to do. I take it -- you're shaking your head, but I take it you were not aware of this particular document?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we -- if we go to the very first page, we have a list of those who are to serve on the presidential council, and would you agree with me that of the eight people that are listed, Jadranko Prlic is not one of them?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, we do see Kresimir Zubak. Did you know Mr. Zubak?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I met Mr. Zubak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. In fact, at some point he replaces Mate Boban, does he not, in that title -- in that position?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. He becomes the president of the Federation, but that is after the Washington Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But you don't know what he became -- what he was before that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough and of course there are other names that you recognise here, like, number 2, we see Akmadzic?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Number 1, Markovic.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perica Jukic. Ante Roso.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Perica Jukic.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivo Lozancic, I recognise those, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But it would appear that Jadranko Prlic at this point in time is not a member of the presidential council of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document would suggest that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And this is signed by the President Mate Boban?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the date is 10 December 1993, while at least at that point in time from your testimony rumours still seem to be circulating as to whether Mate Boban would be in or out, go up or down.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, but it was also clear that on that date he was still the president, and indeed he was presented as such at the Assembly meeting that I went to on the 31st.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. If we go to the next document P 07883. I'm told we need to make two corrections. It should not state "fundamental decision" but, rather, it should be "basic decision of the modification on the amendments of the basic decision on the creation and proclamation of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna." We see this document was generated on 17 February 1994. Were you aware of this particular document which, in a sense, when we see it, we see from Article 8 this legalises essentially the creation and establishment of a presidential council for the Croatian republic?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of this document. I was end of mission and back in England as of this date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Finally I want to share with you one document. It's a rather peculiar document in one way but rather telling in another. It's 1D 01533. And if we flip to the second page we can see it's the official letterhead, or at least it would appear to be the official letterhead of the United Nations Protection Force. It's in B/C/S. At the bottom we see that it is signed by Al Ramsay, Brigadier General. Did you know Mr. Ramsay?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you know of him?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay of the and do you know whether Mr. Ramsay would have been occupying a position with the United Nations Protection Force at or about 20 November 1993?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can't be sure, but don't have any reason to doubt it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And -- now, the content of the letter is not so important. What is important is to whom it is addressed: Union of the republics ever Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Defence Council, and then municipality of Fojnica. Something like that. But here we see the United Nations is addressing its concerns to the union of republics of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and my question I guess would be, and perhaps I'm asking you to speculate - if I am, you tell me so - it would appear that at this point in time the United Nations Protection Force, because of their involvement and perhaps inside information concerning the negotiations, the ongoing negotiations, they are of the opinion that there is a union of the republics of Bosnia-Herzegovina, something that we also see in the preambula or the other documents that refer to or that the Croats are referring to in establishing the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Date of the letter of is a month or so after we see the first establishment. I agree that the headquarters is writing and giving sort of acknowledgement of the Hrvatska Republika Herceg-Bosna. It hadn't been internationally recognised, and yet I guess you're establishing that this letter from UNPROFOR gives it that credibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how Mr. Ramsay got on, if he was questioned by his political masters, but I agree with what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. When you say "internationally recognised," every time you say that, you know, my heart stops a little bit, because it kind of gives the impression that they're trying to create a state that needs international recognition with the flag in New York flying, when in fact we've already agreed that what is being proposed by the Owen-Stoltenberg are republics within a state; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It might be helpful to contrast it with the Bosnian Serb Republic that was set up, again self-styled and not receiving recognition until after the Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I would see that as the equivalence rather than what you described, a separate little state looking for a flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But, you see, in order for us to have this discussion, which is why I started in the beginning, you would have had to know what really transpired in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1992, you know, as -- when you had the winds of war blowing in a southerly direction and where we had this whole discussion in the past year over here, but we'll skip that, because I'm talking about genesis for the creation of the Croatian Community. So since we're -- we've -- you weren't around at that point in time there's no sense in belabouring it but let's go on to some other documents because I think it might be good at this point this time to look at some documents with respect to the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina,, and I'm going to start with 1D 01281. 1D 01281. And this is a decision to accept the documents of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan for Bosnia-Herzegovina. And at the top we see Saturday, 15 May 1993. If we look at Article 1, it says: "The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina hereby accepts in full and shall ensure implementation of the documents of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan for Bosnia and Herzegovina, which was signed on behalf of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina by the president of the Presidency of the RBH as follows," and then it talks about an agreement on Bosnia-Herzegovina signed in Geneva 30 January 1993. Sir, were you aware of this particular decision?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it you were also -- you were also aware of the particular agreement?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and had some understanding about who was enthusiastic in the Vance-Owen Plan and who wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the HDZ -- the Bosnian Croats were enthusiastic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. But also if I -- if I understood your testimony correctly yesterday, and I have it here, I can dig it up someplace, it's here, actually, but -- you did indicate that you, on behalf of ECMM, who were in the process of implementing in some ways the Vance-Owen Peace Plan?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're shaking your head.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That's terribly important that we have this record. That's something that the Judges are tired of hearing me talk about, but it's important. Okay. Now, by the way, were you given instructions on how exactly you were to implement the Vance-Owen Peace Plan? I mean, what concretely you were supposed to do, or was it sort of, you know, self-managing in a sense? Okay, here's a team. Figure it out, come up with a plan, let us know.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was probably more structured than any other that came from the headquarters, but it did leave us discretion on how we supported the development, though clearly, as I said before, we had the framework showing the boundaries and showing the make-up of -- of the cantons and who was to be the president of the cantons. So we busied ourselves trying to organise ECMM to best help deliver the Vance-Owen Plan and part of that was meeting some of the designated members.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay of the and could you tell me about when you started with the implementation?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been when I was HCC Travnik. So that would have been somewhere in about early June, somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now we're going to move very quickly to the next document. 1D 01338.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 1D 01338. So you just focus on the last three numbers.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 1338. This is a conclusion. We see again it's dated 15 of May, 1993. He says, and it's a conclusion, "on the implementation of the documents of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan for Bosnia-Herzegovina." Now, we don't have to spend too much time on -- on "I," just the very first sentence. It says "The Assembly of the republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." We don't need to read that. But if we just go to III on the next -- on the next page, it says: "The Assembly of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina entrusts the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the government of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and other state organs in the republic in accordance with their rights and obligations with taking immediate," I underscore that, "immediate action in adopting necessary measures to implement the documents of the Vance-Owen Plan for Bosnia and Herzegovina." And then it goes on but we don't have time to read it. But we see at the bottom there's a date, 11 May 1993. Were you aware of this particular document, sir?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be sure but we got -- as I say, we did receive instructions and it probably did include this agreement, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now if we could go to another document. 1D 01535. 1535.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've got that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. This is a joint declaration. We see from the very top, "the president of the Republic of Croatia, Dr. Franjo Tudjman." Did you ever meet Dr. Tudjman?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And the president of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Alija Izetbegovic. What about that? Had you ever met Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And did you by any chance talk to him about what his plans were about Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, broadly, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We again. Is that the imperial we or is that ECMM?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the imperial -- no, by imperial I'm referring rather to ECMM. It was the ECMM I took the head of mission to see Mr. Izetbegovic and occasionally we transported him around in our armoured vehicles for meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. You know what I'm talking about when I say the "imperial we"?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps we ought to clarify so there's no --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I mean when the Queen speaks she usually says "we," meaning herself.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, over here it says: "Accepting the principles of the London Conference ..." Did you know what those principles were, sir? Yes, no, I've forgotten?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now if we go to the second page, number, it's important. "One of the joint declarations is to form a working group for matters related for the territorial delimitations between the two republics in the envisaged union of Bosnia-Herzegovina including access to the sea as a matter of common developmental interest." Right around this time I get punchy because I've been up a while. Now, were you aware of this particular joint declaration to form a working group? And here we see, "access to the sea, delimitation between the two republics in the envisaged union." So we're talking about two republics in the union not two states, Bosnia and Croatia, but we're talking about the two republics in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the early foundations of what transpired as the Federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And of course if we go -- and then before we get to the date, if we look at paragraph III.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We see on the second paragraph, Your Honours, that Dr. Franjo Tudjman appoints Dr. Mate Granic, who is the vice-president and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Croatia as his trustee.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Surely you knew or would have known or knew of Dr. Mate Granic; correct?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I do but could you point me to that in the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: III, Okay? Second paragraph, "Dr. -- President Dr. Franjo Tudjman has appointed as his trustee." The same document. It's on the second page, III.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't see it. Must be looking at the wrong bit. Let's just go back and confirm the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The document is 1D 01535.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That explains it; I'm looking at 34. I have the wrong document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You have it?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Go to II, on the second page?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you see Dr. Haris Silajdzic is appointed as President Izetbegovic's trustee, and then if we look at the second page, the third page, I'm sorry, we see it's 14 September 1993, and I believe -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go to the third page in the -- in the B/C/S version, Your Honours, you see signatures over there. And we also have another joint declaration. I'm also reminded that if you go back to I, number 2, paragraph number 2, it says, "provide for the bilateral and unconditional disbanding of all detainee camps and for the release of detainees under control of the army -- of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and HVO immediately by no later than 21 December 1993 -- 21 September 1993, at 1200 hours, and bilaterally assume the responsibility for their protection and care." So this is part of the joint declaration.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it you must have been aware of this?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not this specific document, but the process broadly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, two documents that are of -- that are rather interesting, and we're going to look at them together, but first we'll look at 1D 01436. 1D 01436.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This document was generated as a result of a session that was held on 28 September 1993, and it reads: "Constitutional Law Constituting the Republic of Bosnia." So we're talking about the Republic of Bosnia, not Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And this seems to be a proposal, and we're going to discuss this just very briefly. I'm not suggesting that this was passed, but we have to look at the next document to sort of figure out what exactly they did, but interestingly enough, on -- in Sarajevo, they're proposing for a "Republic of Bosnia that is sovereign and independent state of equal citizens, the Muslim Bosniak nation and member of other nations living in -- living in it based on human rights and civic freedoms, rule of law and social justice." And then you get to Article 2 and it talks about: "The Republic of Bosnia is here by constituted an as a constituent republic of the union of republics of Bosnia and Herzegovina." We go to Article 5. We see that the language -- that the language is, is going to be Bosnian. Article 3, I'm afraid I skipped over this. "Citizens (the Muslim Bosniak nation and members of other nations living in the Republic of Bosnia) --" that's interesting language. "Members of other nations living." And I take it they mean constituent peoples. "... exercise their sovereign rights in the Republic of Bosnia except as otherwise provided in the Constitutional Agreement on the Union of the Republics of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Union of the republics. Now going back to what we had from -- Ramsay was the fellow?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Al.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, were you aware of what was -- were you aware of this particular proposal? Were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but it doesn't surprise or shock me in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we go to Article 6, it talks about -- we see the second sentence. "The borders of the Republic of Bosnia are laid down in the constitutional agreement of the union of republics of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And of course Article 10 may be of some importance but we're not going to discuss it because I need to go to the next document. But just very briefly, were you told at all by your sources and I take it ECMM was also -- was also operating in Sarajevo. Were they informing you of what was happening there?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would get those situation reports but UNPROFOR was operating from Kiseljak so our liaison officer was with the UNPROFOR headquarters, not that -- at this time, actually, in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we look at the next document it's 1D 01532. And so you have to look at both of these together but first we have to look at them separately.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Here we say-- here we see that this is a joint session of the Assembly held on 28 and 29 September 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The previous one was generated on the 28th September, Your Honours. This is the one that comings because there's apparently proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now we look at the conclusions on the draft agreement of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and interestingly -- so if we look at the first -- if we look at the first -- I guess it would be the preambula or -- we see here that this was held on the 27th and 28th of August, 1993. Well, I should read the whole thing I guess. "The Assembly of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, taking into consideration the positions of the Bosniak Assembly, of the political parties and movements, associations of citizens, as well as the opinions of the representatives, have established at the joint Assembly session that the requirements defined at the previous session of the Assembly of RBiH, held on 27 and 28 August 1993, have not been entirely fulfilled. As regards signing of the proposed agreement on Bosnia and Herzegovina, neither have been fulfilled the decisions of the London Conference and the United Nations Resolution on Bosnia and Herzegovina." And in any event, it would appear that at least the proposal, this is in part as a result of the proposal that was presented the previous day, but were you aware of these discussions?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but they're very interesting. I'd love to know who was at that Assembly from Bosnian Croat side, and also interested in the dates, the 28th of August, which I note is the date on which the CRHB was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You know, you read my mind. P 04611. I was going to point you to that, but you led us right to it. Exactly. It seems by serendipity or by design, and I would expect that it's by design, that both sides as result of the ongoing negotiation process and, in an effort to find some sort of a solution, are moving in somewhat of the same direction, in part, although we see at the end the Muslim Bosniak Assembly takes a different position on the 29th of September, 1993, but nonetheless we can see that, at least if we look on paper, and if we look at this that the Croats are not acting independently. They're not trying to get some sort of international recognition in order to carve up, break up Bosnia and Herzegovina, but rather this is an ongoing process, and perhaps one is getting a little ahead of itself over the other, but nonetheless it is a process that both have agreed to participate in. Would that be a correct assessment? Help me out here, and I only have like a minute or so?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that's a good assessment. It shows the fluidity, the various initiatives and helps explain why it was quite a complex picture, which I was trying to gather down in Mostar. We were at a position where various options were being discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: PHILIP ROGER WATKINS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But the idea of there being three republics was being explored, as I've said previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. And we're going to pick up tomorrow where we left off today.
